2020_00_bylaws_ocsba_proposed_amendments.paragraph: Proposed July 2020 amendments to the bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association, distributed to member boards including Troy for the August 18, 2020 meeting. The underlying bylaws carry adoption dates of 11/15/2017 by the Board of Directors and 01/24/2018 and 10/18/2018 by the General Membership, and govern an association whose principal office is 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, Oakland County. The most consequential proposed change adds Article XVI, Section 3, allowing the Board of Directors to set aside bylaw rules governing meetings, elections and the conduct of Association affairs whenever a local, state or national emergency has been declared.
2020_00_bylaws_ocsba_proposed_amendments.page:
**What it is**
Bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association (the "Association"), shown with proposed July 2020 amendments, in the Troy School District Board of Education packet dated August 18, 2020. Adoption lines on the face of the document: Board of Directors 11/15/2017; General Membership 01/24/2018; General Membership 10/18/2018. Sixteen articles across sixteen numbered pages.

**Offices, purpose, dues (Articles I, II, IV)**
Principal office at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, County of Oakland, Michigan, plus a continuously maintained registered office and agent. Eight purposes (a)-(h) run from advancing education quality in Oakland County to sponsoring programs in partnership with Oakland Schools and advocating for county, state and national legislation. Funding is an annual MASB grant to County Area School Boards Association (CASBA) members, ISD dues not exceeding that grant, and contributions and gifts.

**Membership and member meetings (Articles III, V)**
Eligible members are publicly elected Oakland County board of education members or elected Oakland ISD board members in good standing with the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB). Each Member has one in-person vote; on committee-chair selection, resolutions and bylaw amendments each Member School District casts one (1) vote. Electronic voting is reserved to the Board of Directors for emergency business. An annual meeting - the first Regular Meeting after July 1 - plus not less than three additional regular membership meetings are held yearly; member-meeting notice runs not less than ten nor more than fifty days ahead. Quorum is at least one Member from twenty-five (25%) percent of Member School Districts.

**Board and officers (Articles VI-VIII)**
One Member per district may serve at a time, for a three (3) year term. By May 1st an Election Committee of the three most recently elected Directors from different districts is convened; elections occur at the June meeting, by written ballot if candidates exceed vacancies. Missing three (3) consecutive Board meetings constitutes resignation. Board proceedings are confidential. Officers - President (Chief Executive Officer), Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer - are elected from the sitting Board and receive no stated salaries.

**Committees (Article IX)**
| Committee | Meeting frequency | Key deadline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Government Relations | At least 6 times per year | Legislative Priorities to Board by June 15th; chair elected at first meeting after January 31st |
| Resolutions and Bylaws | At least twice per year, amended to once | At least three members appointed by the Board each June |

District voting windows on resolutions and bylaw amendments run at least forty (40) calendar days, and a resolution approved by at least nineteen (19) Member School Districts becomes the Association's official position.

**Financial controls (Article XI)**
Board approval plus signatures of both the President and Treasurer are required for any expenditure exceeding $2,500; expenditures up to $2,500 may be approved by either officer. The Treasurer reports quarterly, presents an annual budget (July 1 to June 30) by June 30th and an annual actual income and expense report by August 30th. Records are reviewed internally by the Board and externally by a third party under agreed-upon procedures, a full audit occurring only if required by law or a third party. An Administrative and Financial Services Agreement with Oakland Schools is permitted.

**Amendments and emergency authority (Article XVI)**
Bylaws are amended by vote of the Member School Districts on written ballots with at least a forty (40) day voting period, one vote per district. Section 2 is amended to allow rules inconsistent with the Articles or Bylaws where a local, state or national emergency has been declared, and a new Section 3 lets the Board set aside bylaw rules on meetings, elections and Association affairs during a declared emergency.
2020_00_bylaws_ocsba_proposed_amendments.verbose:
Bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association, shown with proposed amendments circulated in July 2020 and included in the Troy School District Board of Education materials for August 18, 2020. Three adoption lines head the document: adopted by Board of Directors 11/15/2017; adopted by General Membership 01/24/2018; adopted by General Membership 10/18/2018. The text runs sixteen articles across sixteen numbered pages.

ARTICLE I - OFFICES. The principal office of the Association is at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, County of Oakland, Michigan, with authority to maintain other offices within or outside Michigan. A registered office and a registered agent whose office is identical with it must be continuously maintained; the address may be changed by the Board of Directors.

ARTICLE II - PURPOSE. Eight purposes: advancing the quality of public education in Oakland County through cooperative efforts of locally-elected boards; promoting high standards in programs and services; making information on educational issues available to board members; sponsoring meetings and programs in partnership with Oakland Schools; promoting public understanding of the role of school boards; enhancing cooperation among Oakland County boards; representing those boards to political representatives serving the area; and advocating for county, state and national legislation supporting public education.

ARTICLE III - MEMBERSHIP. Any publicly elected Board of Education member of an Oakland County school district, or any elected Oakland ISD Board of Education member (their districts termed "Member School Districts"), in good standing with the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB), is an eligible general member. Each Member has one vote per matter, cast in person; by exception each Member School District has one (1) vote on selecting a committee chair, on resolutions under Article IX, and on amending the Bylaws under Article XVI. District votes are recorded on receipt of the completed resolution or ballot, must arrive before the stated deadline, and results go to all Member Districts by the next general membership meeting. Electronic voting is granted to the Board of Directors only, for emergency business. Membership is not transferable.

ARTICLE IV - DUES. Financing comes from an annual MASB grant to its County Area School Boards Association (CASBA) members, Intermediate School District membership dues not to exceed the MASB CASBA grant, and contributions and gifts.

ARTICLE V - MEETING OF MEMBERS. An annual meeting plus not less than three additional regular membership meetings occur yearly; the annual meeting is the first Regular Meeting after July 1. Special meetings of the Board or Members may be called by voice or email by the President or by two or more Directors with 30 days' notice. The Secretary delivers written notice personally or by email not less than ten nor more than fifty days before a member meeting. Quorum is at least one Member from twenty-five (25%) percent of the Member School Districts.

ARTICLE VI - ELECTION OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS. Only one Member from each Member School District may serve at a time; the term is three (3) years, continuing until a successor is elected and qualified. By May 1st yearly the Board convenes an Election Committee of the three most recently elected Directors from different Member School Districts (the amendment replaces "create" with "convene"), which seeks candidates giving geographical balance across Oakland County; Candidate Application Forms, formerly "Board Nomination" forms, go to all districts for self-nomination. Additional nominations may come from the floor at the Members' June meeting but not at the meeting where the election occurs; the election is held at the June meeting, by written ballot if candidates exceed vacancies. If candidates are fewer than vacancies the Board appoints a member to serve until the next scheduled election. Directors may resign or be removed with or without cause by majority vote of the Members or Directors then in office, excluding the subject Director; a vacancy is filled by Board appointment for the remainder of the vacated term. Failure to attend three (3) consecutive Board meetings constitutes resignation, subject to an excused absence granted by Board action.

ARTICLE VII - BOARD OF DIRECTORS. The Board carries out the purposes in Article II of the Articles of Incorporation. The regular annual Board meeting needs no notice beyond the Bylaws; special meetings may be called by the President or any two Directors on at least two days' written notice delivered personally, by phone, fax or e-mail, or five days' notice by mail. A majority of Directors is a quorum, and the act of a majority of Directors present serving, whether elected or appointed, is the act of the Board. Directors receive no stated salaries, though a fixed sum and expenses of attendance may be allowed by resolution. Section 9 makes the records and business of all Board proceedings confidential absent advance authorization.

ARTICLE VIII - OFFICERS. The Board elects from its current membership a President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer, serving until the next annual meeting and thereafter until successors are chosen or they resign or are removed by majority vote of the Directors. Officers receive no stated salaries. The President is Chief Executive Officer, manages Association activities, executes authorized conveyances and contracts, and presides at Director meetings. The Secretary records all votes and minutes in a book kept for that purpose. The Treasurer has custody of funds and securities, keeps full and accurate accounts, deposits moneys in designated depositories, disburses funds taking proper vouchers, and if required gives a bond for faithful performance. The Board may require bonds of all officers at Association cost.

ARTICLE IX - COMMITTEES. Standing and ad hoc committees may be designated. The Government Relations Committee is standing, shares legislative information with Member School Districts, and meets at least 6 times per year; each district should appoint a representative at its annual organizational meeting, and a Committee Chairperson is elected annually from the appointed Members at the first committee meeting after January 31st, with one (1) vote per district in attendance. Legislative Priorities are revised annually and submitted to the Board of Directors for approval by June 15th, then provided to the Resolutions and Bylaws Committee and Member School Districts. That committee is also standing and manages the resolutions and bylaws process, meeting at least twice per year with the amendment changing "twice" to "once"; at least three members are appointed by the Board annually in June and elect a Chairperson at their first meeting. Revisions may be initiated by a Member School District Board, the Board of Directors, or either standing committee, and the Board reviews all proposals before they go to Member School Districts, which vote within a window of at least forty (40) calendar days. Resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) Member School Districts become the official position of the Association.

ARTICLE X - DISSOLUTION. Assets are distributed as provided in Article VIII of the Articles of Incorporation. No net earnings may inure to any Member, Director or Officer, as prohibited by Section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, the Michigan General Sales Tax Act or the Michigan Use Tax Act.

ARTICLE XI - FIDUCIARY AND FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITIES. Expenditures may not exceed the approved annual budget, and no committee may create financial liability unless authorized by a majority of the Members. Board approval and signatures of both the President and Treasurer are required for any expenditure exceeding $2,500; expenditures up to $2,500 must be approved by either the Board President or the Treasurer, with the Vice President substituting if either is absent or disabled. Reports go to all Board members quarterly or on request; the Treasurer presents an annual budget covering July 1 to June 30 by June 30th and an annual actual income and expense report by August 30th, both presented at the first fall Member Meeting, with records closed annually for IRS filings. Agreed-upon procedures are performed annually by the Board internally and by a third party externally, an audit occurring only if required by law or a third party. Section 4 permits an Administrative and Financial Services Agreement with Oakland Schools, monitored by the Treasurer.

ARTICLE XII - INDEMNIFICATION. Directors and officers are indemnified to the fullest extent authorized by the Michigan Nonprofit Association Act, for third-party claims and claims brought by or in the right of the Association, covering expenses, attorneys' fees, judgments, penalties, fines and settlements where the Indemnitee acted in good faith; claims brought by the Indemnitee are excluded unless authorized by the Board. Determinations are made by majority vote of a quorum of non-party directors, by a committee of not less than two (2) disinterested directors, or by independent legal counsel in a written opinion. Expenses are advanced on an unsecured unlimited general obligation undertaking to repay, and the Association may purchase liability insurance.

ARTICLES XIII-XV. The fiscal year is set by the Board of Directors. The conflicts article requires officers, directors, committee members and employees to avoid conflicts; a contract with an interested director is not void solely for that interest if it is fair and reasonable or if material facts are disclosed and it is approved without counting that director's vote. A conflicted Director must give notice, refrain from voting, is excluded from the quorum on that matter, and the minutes must reflect the disclosure and abstention. Miscellaneous provisions govern conveyances, execution of checks, drafts, bills of exchange, acceptances and notes, borrowing, adjourned meetings, notice by mail, written consent filed with the minutes, participation by conference telephone constituting presence in person, and a corporate seal inscribed with the Association name, "Corporate Seal" and "Michigan."

ARTICLE XVI - AMENDMENTS AND ADDITIONS. Bylaws may be altered or amended by vote of the Member School Districts, with the Board providing a written ballot and at least a forty (40) day voting period, one vote per district. Section 2, on additional rules for Board meetings and Association affairs, is amended to insert "unless a local, state or national emergency has been declared" before the bar on rules inconsistent with the Articles of Incorporation or Bylaws. A new Section 3, "Rules and Regulations During a Declared Emergency," provides that on a declared local, state or national emergency the Board of Directors may set aside rules and regulations within the bylaws, general or specific, regarding the conduct of their meetings and election and the conduct of the affairs of the Association.

2020_01_june_2020_financial_statements.paragraph: Unaudited statements of revenues and expenditures for Troy School District covering the year ended June 30, 2020, presented to the Board of Education on August 18, 2020 and compared against the budget column dated 6/16/20. The General Fund (Funds 101, 120 and 122) recorded total revenues of $157,721,914 against a budget of $160,466,086 and total expenditures of $157,056,493 against $159,107,325, producing revenues over expenditures of $665,421. Companion statements cover consolidated debt service, special revenue and capital projects funds; the capital projects group reported expenditures of $21,230,038 and revenues under expenditures of $7,050,162.

General Fund revenue of $872,557 - all of it from local sources, at 0.58% of the $151,057,442 budget - trailed expenditures of $2,120,688, leaving revenues under expenditures of $1,248,131. Capital projects were the outlier: capital outlay of $3,729,148 had already been spent against a $16,515,646 budget.

2020_03_5_g_cares_act_oakland_county_int.paragraph: Interlocal agreement between Oakland County and the Troy School District distributing a share of the county's federal CARES Act money through the Oakland Together Schools COVID Support Fund, brought to the Board of Education as agenda item 5.G on October 20, 2020. Entered under the Urban Cooperation Act of 1967, 1967 Public Act 7, MCL 124.501 et seq., it reimburses only pandemic costs absent from the district's budget as approved on March 27, 2020, never revenue losses. Treasury guidance presumes eligibility up to $500 per student without itemization; anything above that cap requires detailed records. The agreement runs until January 31, 2021, with Expenditure Submission Forms accepted only through November 30, 2020.
2020_03_5_g_cares_act_oakland_county_int.page:
**Parties and authority**
Agreement for CARES Act Distribution between Oakland County, a Municipal and Constitutional Corporation, 1200 North Telegraph Road, Pontiac, Michigan 48341, and the Troy School District, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Executed under the Urban Cooperation Act of 1967, 1967 Public Act 7, MCL 124.501 et seq. Board of Education agenda item 5.G, October 20, 2020.

**What is being distributed**
CARES Act funds are money distributed to the County by the United States Department of Treasury under section 601(a) of the Social Security Act, as added by section 5001 of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act. The portion allocated to school districts is the Oakland Together Schools COVID Support Fund. The Office of the Oakland County Executive (OCE) reviews each Expenditure Submission Form and works with the Board of Commissioners Oversight Committee on eligibility.

**County responsibilities**
- OCE determines eligibility at its discretion under the Coronavirus Relief Fund Guidance for State, Territorial, Local and Tribal Governments, and may request supporting documentation.
- A distribution cap is set for each district based on enrolled students, teachers employed, and students eligible for the federal free and reduced lunch program; the cap is not a guarantee.
- No Expenditure Submission Forms are accepted after November 30, 2020; unclaimed balances are retained and may be redistributed to other eligible districts.

**District responsibilities**
Eligible expenses are limited to costs incurred due to the COVID-19 public health emergency: distance-learning facilitation including technological improvements tied to school closings, acquisition and distribution of medical and protective supplies, disinfection of public areas and facilities, and compliance with COVID-19 public health orders. Funds may only cover expenses not accounted for in the district's most recently approved budget as of March 27, 2020, and may not be used as revenue replacement. Under Treasury guidance the district submits documentation of CARES money already received up to the $500 per-pupil allowable cap and requests the remaining per-pupil amount; requests above the $500 per-pupil administrative cap require records of all excess expenditures with a detailed description of use and compliance. Records must be kept a minimum of 10 (ten) years and produced on request or on audit. Duplicate federal or state funding, and any spending found non-compliant, must be returned to the County.

**Term and termination**
Effective on execution by both Parties with resolutions of their governing bodies, entered in official minutes, and filed by the County Clerk with the Secretary of State. In effect until January 31, 2021 unless cancelled; record-keeping, reporting, audit-response and fund-return duties survive termination. The County may terminate for misuse, with repayment owed; the district may terminate at any time and must immediately return all funds received.

**Legal terms**
Each Party bears its own claims, legal representation and costs; there is no indemnification and no waiver of governmental immunity. Assignment requires prior written consent. No third-party beneficiaries. Governed by Michigan law with venue in the 6th Judicial Circuit Court, the 50th District Court, or the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, Southern Division. Notices go to the Oakland County Executive at 2100 Pontiac Lake Rd., Waterford, MI 48328 and the Chairperson of the Oakland County Board of Commissioners at 1200 North Telegraph Road, Pontiac, MI 48341, and to the School District Superintendent at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098.

**Signatures**
Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, signs for Troy School District under a Board of Education resolution, witnessed by Rick West, Assistant Superintendent. David Woodward, Chairperson of the Oakland County Board of Commissioners, signs for the County.
2020_03_5_g_cares_act_oakland_county_int.verbose:
Agreement for CARES Act Distribution between Oakland County and the Troy School District, carried as item 5.G on the Troy School District Board of Education agenda for October 20, 2020. The County is identified as a Municipal and Constitutional Corporation at 1200 North Telegraph Road, Pontiac, Michigan 48341; the School District at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. The agreement is entered pursuant to the Urban Cooperation Act of 1967, 1967 Public Act 7, MCL 124.501 et seq., for the purpose of the County distributing a portion of its CARES Act funds to school districts within Oakland County to assist them in meeting areas of need caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

DEFINITIONS. "CARES Act funds" means money distributed to the County by the United States Department of Treasury pursuant to section 601(a) of the Social Security Act, as added by section 5001 of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act. "Oakland Together Schools COVID Support Fund" means the portion of those CARES Act funds the County has allocated to school districts within Oakland County. "Expenditure Submission Form" is the form the district must complete and submit to OCE before any disbursement. "OCE" means the Office of the Oakland County Executive, including the Chief Deputy and other Deputy County Executives. "Oversight Committee" means the committee established by the Oakland County Board of Commissioners in the resolution allocating the Oakland Together Schools funds. "Day" means any calendar day beginning at 12:00 a.m. and ending at 11:59 p.m. "Claims" is defined expansively to cover losses, complaints, demands, lawsuits, causes of action, judgments, deficiencies, liabilities, penalties, litigation, costs and expenses including reimbursement for reasonable attorney fees, witness fees, court costs, investigation and litigation expenses and settlement amounts. "County" includes all departments, divisions, the County Board of Commissioners, elected and appointed officials, directors, board members, council members, commissioners, authorities, committees, employees, agents and volunteers. "School District" includes its school board, superintendent, employees, agents, subcontractors, attorneys and volunteers. "School District Employee" reaches officers, directors, members, managers, trustees, volunteers, attorneys, representatives, licensees, concessionaires, contractors, subcontractors, independent contractors and agents who use or access the funds, including former employees during the term, but excludes an individual resident who receives an authorized distribution.

COUNTY RESPONSIBILITIES (Section 2). OCE reviews the district's Expenditure Submission Form to determine eligibility, exercising discretion under the "Coronavirus Relief Fund Guidance for State, Territorial, Local and Tribal Government" or other federal guidance, and may request any supporting documentation it deems necessary. If eligible, the County distributes the eligible amount. The County sets a distribution cap for each district based on three factors: the number of students enrolled in the district, the number of teachers employed by the district, and the number of students eligible for the federal free and reduced lunch program; the cap is expressly not a guarantee or promise of a certain amount. The County has no obligation to distribute funds if OCE finds the district ineligible or if available funds are insufficient to fulfill the submitted form. Under Section 2.5, after November 30, 2020 the County will not accept any further Expenditure Submission Forms, and will retain the balance of funds for which the district was originally eligible but which are not covered by an approved form; the County may then redistribute any or all of that retained amount to other eligible school districts or as otherwise deemed appropriate by OCE. OCE works in collaboration with the Board of Commissioners Oversight Committee in determining eligibility and amounts.

SCHOOL DISTRICT RESPONSIBILITIES (Section 3). The district must complete and submit an Expenditure Submission Form and obtain OCE approval before any distribution. It must follow all United States Treasury Department and County guidance, including Section 601(d) of the Social Security Act and the Coronavirus Relief Fund Guidance. Funds may be spent only on expenses incurred due to the COVID-19 public health emergency, such as expenses to facilitate distance learning including technological improvements in connection with school closings to enable compliance with COVID-19 precautions; expenses for the acquisition and distribution of medical and protective supplies; expenses for disinfection of public areas and other facilities; and expenses to ensure compliance with COVID-19 public health orders. Spending is further restricted to expenses not accounted for in the district's most recently approved budget as of March 27, 2020, and the funds may not be used as revenue replacement. Per Treasury guidance quoted in the agreement - "as an administrative convenience, Treasury will presume that expenses of up to $500 per elementary and secondary school student to be eligible expenditures, such that schools do not need to document the specific use of funds up to that amount" - the district submits documentation of how much CARES Act money it has already received up to the $500 allowable cap and requests the remaining amount per pupil from the County. Any request above the $500 per pupil administrative cap requires the district to submit records of all expenditures in excess of that amount to OCE before reimbursement, with a detailed description of how funds were expended and how the expenditure complied with CARES Act requirements. If the district receives federal or state funding covering the same expenses, it must return that amount to the County. Records sufficient to demonstrate compliance must be kept for a minimum of 10 (ten) years and produced on request by the County or OCE or as required by any future CARES Act audit. Any amount found by OCE or any audit to have been expended in violation of the CARES Act or the agreement must be returned to the County.

DURATION (Section 4). The agreement is effective when executed by both Parties with resolutions passed by their governing bodies where applicable; its approval and terms are entered in the official minutes of each governing body, and an executed copy plus any amendments is filed by the County Clerk with the Secretary of State. It remains in effect until January 31, 2021 unless cancelled or terminated earlier, and the district must comply with record keeping, reporting, audit response and fund return requirements after termination.

ASSURANCES (Section 5). Each Party is responsible for Claims made against it by third parties and for the acts of its employees. Except as provided in Section 3.13, each Party seeks its own legal representation and bears its own costs including judgments and attorney fees. There is no right to indemnification or reimbursement between the Parties. The district is solely responsible for all costs, fines and fees associated with any misuse of the funds or noncompliance by School District Employees. The agreement does not impair, divest, delegate or contravene any constitutional, statutory or other legal right, privilege, power, obligation, duty or immunity, and nothing constitutes a waiver of governmental immunity. Both Parties confirm they have taken all actions and secured all approvals necessary and that their signatories have legal authority to bind them. Each Party must comply with all applicable federal, state and local ordinances, regulations and administrative rules.

TERMINATION (Section 6). The County may terminate or cancel at any time if it determines the district spent funds in violation of the CARES Act or the agreement, with either OCE or the Board of Commissioners authorized to act, and the district then liable to repay the amount spent in violation. The district may terminate at any time if it does not wish to receive funds, in which case it must immediately return all funds already received. Written notice under Section 13 is required from either Party.

REMAINING TERMS. Section 7 bars delegation or assignment without prior written consent; Section 8 creates no third-party beneficiaries; Section 9 requires a written waiver; Section 10 severs illegal or invalid terms; Section 11 gives the Agreement precedence over conflicting documents; Section 12 makes captions non-substantive. Section 13 requires written notices, personally delivered or sent by express delivery service, certified mail, or first class U.S. mail postage prepaid, deemed given on actual receipt, the next business day for express or personal delivery, or three days after mailing; County notices go to the Oakland County Executive, 2100 Pontiac Lake Rd., Waterford, MI, 48328, and the Chairperson of the Oakland County Board of Commissioners, 1200 North Telegraph Road, Pontiac, MI, 48341, and district notices to the School District Superintendent, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Section 14 applies Michigan law with venue in the 6th Judicial Circuit Court of the State of Michigan, the 50th District Court of the State of Michigan, or the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, Southern Division. Section 15 lists surviving terms: Definitions (Section 1), Assurances (Section 5), No Third-Party Beneficiaries (Section 8), No Implied Waiver (Section 9), Severability (Section 10), Precedence of Documents (Section 11), Governing Law/Consent to Jurisdiction and Venue (Section 14), Survival of Terms (Section 15), Entire Agreement (Section 16), and the record keeping, reporting, audit compliance and fund return provisions of Section 3. Section 16 makes the agreement the entire understanding regarding the Oakland Together Schools COVID Support funds, superseding all other oral or written agreements on that subject.

EXECUTION. Dr. Rich Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, acknowledges authorization by a resolution of the Troy School District Board of Education, a certified copy of which is attached, to execute the agreement and bind the district; the witness line names Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Troy School District. David Woodward, Chairperson of the Oakland County Board of Commissioners, acknowledges authorization by a resolution of the Oakland County Board of Commissioners to execute on behalf of Oakland County. Execution and date lines are left blank in the packet copy.
